title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault‑Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692308, 0.35897436] (bootstrap resamples = 10 000, seed = 1729). Execution used declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). A preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory executor; the preregistered harmful-change mapping and the per-episode traces required to compute that aggregation are archived and the exact reproduction path is documented in Methods and the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are being explored to assist network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A safety-oriented pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior empirical results in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings report that verifier-interposed repair can raise verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Survey and field work in NetOps/AIOps contexts caution that read-oriented assistance does not automatically translate to safe closed-loop changes [5].

Research question and contribution. Controlled paired evidence for verifier-guided repair applied to vendor CLI templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is scarce. Because an intervention can only act when an initial candidate triggers actionable diagnostics, we run a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault challenge in a paired design that reuses the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? We contribute (a) a preregistered paired controlled-challenge execution using adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics (planned n = 40), (b) a complete, artifact-grounded primary confirmatory analysis showing a substantial guarded > baseline improvement on the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate, and (c) a transparent account of a preregistered confirmatory safety aggregation (harmful-overrepair) that the archived confirmatory executor did not produce together with exact artifact locations and an operational mapping so auditors can deterministically reproduce it.
sections.related_work:
Empirical GVR evidence in adjacent domains. Controlled program-repair and IaC studies report that inserting deterministic verifiers between generation and acceptance can materially increase verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair model improves the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [1], [2]. These works demonstrate that compact mechanically-checkable predicates can serve as useful repair signals in domains with executable validators.

Caveats from recent analyses. Controlled analyses have shown that single-proxy verifier iterative refinement can be exploited ("verifier-exploitation") where optimization toward the proxy reduces fidelity to the underlying target property; mitigation strategies and careful pipeline design are advised [3]. Studies of verifier-mediated agent pipelines also measure a nontrivial interaction overhead (a "verifier tax") that affects cost/latency tradeoffs [4].

NetOps domain positioning. Surveys and demonstration-network case studies find LLMs useful for read-oriented NetOps tasks but warn against assuming safe autonomous changes without robust verification and conservative orchestration [5]. These gaps motivated our preregistered controlled-challenge paired design: deterministic fault injection to ensure intervention informativeness, shared-source pairing to identify the causal effect of exposing diagnostics, and frozen harmful-change rules to operationalize safety auditing.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where success requires both deterministic vendor-CLI verifier acceptance (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator-based compliance agreement (verifier+simulator). The preregistration SHA-256 is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 0ba66573928647f008b2cd5b9dde6708a61ae86ece55b693ace534e01e2b132c).

Adapter semantics and pairing. Confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate (deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1) was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial sampled generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The adapter-mandated confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40. The execution manifest records: planned_episode_count = 80, completed_episode_count = 78, complete_pair_count = 39, model_calls_used = 118, maximum_model_calls = 120, source_generation_attempt_count = 40 (source_valid_count = 39, source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). These paths and counts are archived in the execution manifest referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

Runtime sampling records and temperature. The archived model configuration declares requested_model = gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset) in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call runtime sampling parameters and provider call metadata are available in the archived provider-call traces and execution log (execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*) recorded in the execution manifest; auditors may inspect those per-call records to reconstruct sampling behavior for each hosted-model call.

Controlled-challenge informativeness and missingness rules. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (examples: dropped_required_restore, protected_interface_change). The preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' excludes a pair only if both condition executions are unscorable; this occurred once (both_missing_pairs = 1) and is documented in analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring, harmful-change mapping, and reproducibility. The primary acceptance predicate required both the deterministic verifier and a simulator agreement. The preregistered harmful-change labeling schema (used to operationalize the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory hypothesis) is archived as a transformation artifact (execution/transformation_manifest.json). Compact operational mapping for auditors: label an episode harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains either PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE. The per-episode fields validation_after.violation_codes are present in execution/scoring/*.json and execution/raw_results.jsonl. The confirmatory analysis executor archived the primary paired counts but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; exact artifact locations and the mapping above permit deterministic reproduction by independent auditors following the preregistered analysis pipeline.

Statistical analysis. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial) on the combined success indicator. We report discordant-pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10 000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity: a single predefined primary test (no multiplicity adjustment); per-fault-class summaries are exploratory. Missingness sensitivity: primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs per 'complete_pair_primary'; a sensitivity analysis treating missing episodes as failures is archived but reported separately.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary confirmatory outcomes. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs), failed_episode_count = 2, hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (39 valid, 1 invalid). Run timestamps and artifact paths are recorded in the execution manifest; key archived analysis artifacts include analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (hashes recorded in the evidence manifest).

Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589744. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051282051. Exact two-sided paired test: p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692308, 0.35897436] (bootstrap_resamples = 10 000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). These tabulations and CSV artifacts are archived at analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded under 'complete_pair_primary' because the source-generation attempt for its task index was invalid and produced two unscorable condition episodes (both_missing_pairs = 1). Per-episode terminal error records and logs are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl for auditing.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis bounding any absolute increase in harmful-overrepair (harmful-change mapping uses validator violation codes PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE). The archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute that preregistered aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because it was not produced by the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim. Instead we provide the exact reproducibility path: (1) iterate the 39 complete pairs (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), (2) for each episode read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl), (3) compute per-episode harmful indicator using the compact mapping above, and (4) compute paired counts and the same exact paired test and bootstrap CI per the analysis plan. All required per-episode fields and transformation artifacts are archived; independent auditors may deterministically reproduce the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation from those artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The preregistered paired result shows a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. Because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets, the contrast isolates the effect of exposing diagnostics. Archived per-episode scoring traces illustrate concrete mechanisms: diagnostics often identify protected fields or unintended-state changes (validator_trace.violation_codes), and exposing those diagnostics to the model appears to guide targeted corrective edits that blind repair sometimes omitted (examples archived at execution/scoring/task-000002-*.json and task-000003-*.json).

Safety boundary and unresolved confirmatory aggregation. The preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory test remains unresolved in the archived confirmatory summary because that aggregation was not computed by the archived executor. We do not convert an exploratory recomputation into a confirmatory claim; instead we document the exact artifact locations and the operational harmful-change mapping that permit deterministic independent reconstruction.

Operational considerations and verifier tax. Instrumentation shows the verifier-guided workflow requires additional interactions (hosted-model calls = 118; stage_counts recorded in provider_call_audit). These counts permit exploratory cost-per-avoided-failure calculations, but generalizing cost/latency tradeoffs to operational deployments requires larger-scale experimentation. Verifier coverage is critical: a verifier cannot improve what it cannot detect, and narrow verifier coverage risks overfitting repairs to its detectable surface. Prior literature warns of verifier-exploitation in long-horizon iterative pipelines; our short-horizon, single-repair-budget, shared-candidate pairing reduces that exposure but does not eliminate it—multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change enforcement, abstention, and uncertainty quantification are plausible mitigations.

Threats to validity. Internal: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature = null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair constrain claims about generation determinism; runtime per-call sampling parameters are archived for inspection (execution/execution_log.jsonl and provider traces). Construct: primary success depends on agreement between a deterministic verifier and a simulator; both components limit the operational meaning of "valid". External: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic template-based controlled faults constrain generalization. Conclusion: complete_pairs = 39 yields a reasonably precise primary contrast but limits fine-grained subgroup inference; per-fault-class explorations are exploratory.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692308, 0.35897436]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not computed by the archived confirmatory executor and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the artifact bundle includes the exact transformation and per-episode traces required for deterministic independent reconstruction. We release the archived artifacts to enable reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies before operational deployment.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration_sha256 recorded in execution manifest). Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: execution manifest records temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Harmful-change mapping and reconstructability: the preregistered harmful-change rules were frozen and the transformation artifact implementing the mapping is archived (see execution/transformation_manifest.json and the full artifact manifest execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Per-episode raw traces and scoring artifacts required to reproduce all aggregated confirmatory and preregistered secondary statistics are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv). The study followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
